normal: A grain map whose grain colors are random and spread evenly over the whole color spectrum; no hue or hue family is more common than the others, and similar colors do not cluster together.
defective: A grain map in which grain colors are not evenly spread: one or two hue families (for example reds, or reds and cyans) are clearly more common than the rest, or grains of similar color cluster in patches or bands.
